module.purpose: Defines the primary React Flow container component, wiring graph data, interaction callbacks, viewport behavior, accessibility, styling, and internal store synchronization into the rendered flow canvas.
module.summary: This module is the composition boundary for a React Flow application. It accepts generic node and edge data plus extensive interaction and viewport configuration, derives container identity and color-mode styling, restores the wrapper scroll position, and composes internal updater, rendering, selection, attribution, and accessibility components. The public component is exposed through a ref-forwarding wrapper.
module.businessContext: Supports interactive node-and-edge diagrams in React applications. Failure prevents graph rendering, user interactions, viewport control, selection, and accessibility behavior from reaching consumers.
functions: ReactFlow (~L24-329): Composes graph state, interaction handlers, viewport configuration, and accessibility components
wrapperOnScroll (~L161-168): Resets wrapper scrolling before forwarding the scroll event
systemCapabilities: Synchronize graph props with internal state
Handle node, edge, pane, and selection events
Configure panning, zooming, and viewport constraints

preconditions: The props argument conforms to ReactFlowProps<NodeType, EdgeType>.
The forwarded ref is a valid React ref target or null.
postconditions: Returns an outer div with data-testid="rf__wrapper", role="application", the supplied id, merged class names, and merged style.
The supplied graph configuration and children are rendered within the React Flow wrapper.
If an onScroll callback is supplied, it is invoked after the wrapper scroll position is reset to top 0 and left 0.
invariants: The internal React Flow identifier is the supplied id when truthy, otherwise '1'.
The outer wrapper always includes the base class 'react-flow' and the color-mode class.
The forwarded ref is attached to the outer wrapper div.
The wrapper's scroll handler always attempts to restore scroll position to { top: 0, left: 0, behavior: 'instant' } before forwarding the event.
edgeCases: When id is absent or falsy, descendants receive the fallback React Flow identifier '1', while the outer div receives the original id value.
When className or style is absent, the base/color-mode classes and wrapper style still render; supplied class names and styles are merged with them.
When onScroll is absent, scrolling still resets the wrapper position and no callback is invoked.
When children are absent, the built-in graph, selection listener, attribution, and accessibility description elements are still rendered.
detail.summary: Renders the React Flow application container and wires the supplied node, edge, viewport, interaction, accessibility, and callback configuration into the graph view. It exposes the outer HTML div through the forwarded ref and prevents wrapper scrolling from shifting the viewport.

specTests.when: The outer wrapper receives a scroll event.
specTests.then: The wrapper invokes scrollTo with { top: 0, left: 0, behavior: 'instant' } and then invokes the supplied onScroll callback with the same event.
The outer div has id="flow-a", includes the classes "react-flow", "custom", and the dark color-mode class, and has role="application".
The descendants that consume rfId receive the fallback identifier "1", while the outer div's id prop remains the supplied falsy value.
